predecessors.name: United Provinces of New Granada
predecessors.text: New Granada, 'unexpected victory' of Bolivar; the 1819 Cundinamarca department 'became the core' of the later Republic of New Granada

predecessors.name: Spanish Empire
predecessors.text: Venezuela (Carabobo), Panama (November 1821), and the provinces of Pasto, Guayaquil and Quito (1822)

successors.name: Republic of New Granada
successors.text: the central departments (Boyaca, Cauca, Cundinamarca, Magdalena, Isthmus) that became the State of New Granada

successors.name: Venezuela
successors.text: Venezuela's constituent congress at Valencia: autonomy 6 May 1830, definitive separation 22 September 1830

successors.name: Republic of Ecuador
successors.text: the departments of Ecuador, Guayaquil and Azuay, the State of Ecuador of 13 May 1830

ledger.x: 1819: Gran Colombia is proclaimed at Angostura.
1822: the Peruvian provinces of the claim appear in Cliopatria's shape.

wars.name: Gran Colombia-Peru War
wars.outcome: Stalemate after Tarqui; the Armistice of Piura (10 July 1829) recognised Guayaquil as Gran Colombian and Tumbes, Jaen and Maynas as Peruvian; the Larrea-Gual Treaty (22 September 1829) ended the war with 'status quo ante bellum' and a boundary commission.

wars.name: Paez's revolt in Venezuela
wars.outcome: Paez mutinied on 30 April 1826, was amnestied, and led Venezuela out of the union in 1829-1830 (Valencia congress, 6 May and 22 September 1830).

certainty.note: The republic's claim rested on uti possidetis and colonial boundaries the Peru war page calls imprecise; the Peruvian, Brazilian and Essequibo frontiers were never fixed (the 1829 treaty left the Peruvian line to a commission).
